labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/1-causality
labels.notes: Checked against the target's title and evidence (programme/roadmap.toml:1045-1055). The coordinates are (t, x) = (p.1, p.2). RationalJumpCausal a b (:105) is a.2 - b.2 <= b.1 - a.1 and b.2 - a.2 <= b.1 - a.1, i.e. |dx| <= dt, a future causal segment. RationalJumpChronal (:109) is the same with strict inequalities, |dx| < dt. IsRationalJump (:113) is equal t, a.2 < b.2, and both x-coordinates in range of the cast from Q. Each step carries segment R a b inside U, which for a jump is exactly {t} x [q, q'] inside U. The relations: le U := TransGen (rationalJumpStep U) and lt U := TransGen (rationalJumpChronalStep U). That is the target's 'chains of causal segments or rational jumps in U' and 'chains of timelike segments in U', with nothing added. Every field of the library Causality is discharged honestly. Membership comes from the segment ends. le_refl uses a trivial causal step whose segment is {x}. Transitivity is TransGen.trans, monotony is inclusion of segments, and le_of_lt goes step by step. isOpen_lt_right/left move the last or first chronal step: strict inequalities are open, and eventually_segment_subset_of_isOpen keeps the segment in U. Non-degeneracy: le_M lies strictly between the chains of Minkowski causal segments and {dt >= 0, d(t+x) >= 0} (rationalJumpPlane_le_imp). It contains (0,0) <= (0,1), which is not Minkowski-causal. My probe proved (0,0) <= (1,0), not (1,0) <= (0,0), and not (0,1) <= (0,0). At equal t it is exactly the rational line's relation, so (0,0) and (0, v) with v irrational are incomparable. So the jumps make le neither total nor empty. Every positive property needed a real argument: the shift for causal openness, the box in (t, t+x) for strong causality, the Lebesgue subdivision for minimality. Every negative one rests on one specific jump, not on a vacuous curve notion: CurveOn is the library's, and vertical lines are causal curves.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/2-absolutely-minimal
labels.notes: #print Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn: for every cover S of W and every V <= W, both le V and lt V are TransGen of relations localised in V ⊓ O, O in S. rationalJumpPlane_absolutelyMinimalOn (:358) proves it for every W and both halves. That is the gluing reading of defi:causalite (OQ-18, as in kb/0074 and OQ-69). rationalJumpPlane_absolutelyMinimal (:395), the ladder's node Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal of .toPrecausality, follows by Precausality.absolutelyMinimal_iff (Generated.lean:275: AbsolutelyMinimal <-> AbsolutelyMinimalOn ⊤). The delicate point checks out. In transGen_of_segment_subdivision (:293) the hypothesis hR quantifies over c1 c2 : Q only, with 0 <= c1 < c2 <= 1. The nodes are p j = a + (((j:Q)/n : Q) : R) • (b - a), with n > ||b - a|| / delta and delta a Lebesgue number of the cover {V ⊓ O} of the compact segment (lebesgue_number_lemma_of_metric). Each piece [p k, p (k+1)] has length ||b - a||/n < delta, so it lies in ball(p k, delta), hence in one V ⊓ O. IsRationalJump.sub (:277) takes rational c1 < c2 and produces the rational ends q + c1(q' - q) and q + c2(q' - q). So the pieces of a jump are jumps, and the pieces of causal and timelike segments are causal and timelike at any parameter (:255, :266). This is the rational line's route (rationalLine_absolutelyMinimal, NestedConverse.lean:303), not cor:causalement_connexe_minimal, as the REPORT says. The metric tools (Lebesgue number, ball, norm) are inside proofs only. The statement of transGen_of_segment_subdivision uses segments, Opens and V ⊓ O, nothing metric.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/3-chronal-neighbours
labels.notes: #print Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours = ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ dual.ChronalPastNeighbours: every v in every open V has p in V with p ≪_V v, and p' in V with v ≪_V p'. The proof takes a ball of radius rho about v inside V. It joins (t - rho/2, x) to v, and v to (t + rho/2, x), by one vertical timelike segment each (dt = rho/2 > 0 = |dx|), inside the convex ball. The directions are right for both halves. Tarentin then follows by the library's ChronalNeighbours.tarentin.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/4-time-function
labels.notes: Causal.Causality.HasTimeFunction = ∃ T continuous, ∀ x y, le ⊤ x y → x ≠ y → T x < T y. T = 2t + x, the evidence's t + x/2 doubled, which is an equivalent choice. Along a causal segment 2dt + dx >= dt >= 0, with equality only if dt = 0, which forces dx = 0. Along a jump it rises by dx > 0. So rationalJumpStep.eq_or_lt and rationalJumpPlane_le_eq_or_lt are correct. IsCausal comes by HasTimeFunction.isCausal, and CurvesExtend by HasTimeFunction.curvesExtend, inside the separation.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/5-not-arc-connected
labels.notes: #print Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnectedOn W: ∀ U <= W, ∀ p q, (le U p q <-> ∃ c, CausalCurveOn U c 0 1 ∧ c 0 = p ∧ c 1 = q), and the same for lt. rationalJumpPlane_le_zero_one is one jump with q = 0, q' = 1 and the segment inside ⊤. rationalJumpPlane_causalCurveOn_eq (:478) is correct. t is constant along the curve by le_imp in both directions, so between two of its points le is equality or a rational jump. If x(γ s) < x(γ s'), the IVT gives an r with x(γ r) = v irrational. Then γ s <= γ r at equal t is neither an equality nor a jump with a rational end, a contradiction. This is the rational line's argument (rationalLine_causalCurveOn_eq, NestedConverse.lean:279) transported to the slice. The conclusion is stronger than the target's: no causal curve of any open W, over any s0 <= s1, joins (0,0) to (0,1) (rationalJumpPlane_zero_one_separates). The claim that no non-empty open set is causally arc-connected also checks out (rationalJumpPlane_not_causallyArcConnectedOn, :553). For m in W, exists_rationalJump_chronal puts a jump (m.1, q) -> (m.1, q') inside a ball in W, with q < q' rational. Arc-connectedness on W, applied with U = W, would turn it into a causal curve over [0, 1]. That curve is constant, so q = q', a contradiction. Not locally arc-connected follows at x = 0 with N = univ.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/6-not-push-up
labels.notes: #print Causal.Causality.PushUpOn W: ∀ U <= W, (lt;le => lt) ∧ (le;lt => lt). In every open W about m: (m.1, q) <=_W (m.1, q') by a jump, and (m.1, q') ≪_W (m.1 + (q' - q)/2, q') by a vertical timelike segment. The composite ≪ would need dx = q' - q < dt = (q' - q)/2, which is impossible (rationalJumpPlane_lt_imp). This is a stronger form of the evidence's triple (0,0) <= (0,1) ≪ (1, 3/2), which is the case W = M (checked by hand: (0,1) ≪ (1,3/2) since 1/2 < 1, and not (0,0) ≪ (1,3/2) since 3/2 > 1). ¬PushUp comes via pushUpOn_top. ¬LocallyPushUp is direct at 0, since every W about 0 fails. ¬CausallyPlain comes by causal_ladder, read backwards through absolutely_minimal ∧ causally_plain ⇒ push_up (T1 on R × R).

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/7-ladder
labels.notes: Beyond the target, every part proved. CausallyOpen is the library's two-sided form (Properties.lean:130). For y in J+_U(V) from x in V, the chain is shifted by (s, 0) with s < 0 small. rationalJumpStep.eventually_shift: the step kinds are invariant under time translation, a jump keeps its rational x-ends, and the shifted segment stays in a thickening of the compact segment inside U. Then x + (s,0) is in V, with x + (s,0) <=_U y + (s,0) ≪_U y, and I+_U(y + (s,0)) is an open neighbourhood of y inside J+_U(V). The past moves upward. I checked the argument and it is sound. StronglyCausalOpen: the box |t - p.1| < rho/2, |(t + x) - (p.1 + p.2)| < rho/2 is open and lies in the sup-metric ball of radius rho. It is causally convex in ⊤ because t and t + x are monotone along <=. ¬CausallyCompact: compactness, hence closedness in T2, of J_M((0,0),(0,1)) would make its slice at t = 0 closed. That slice contains (0, q) for every rational q in (0,1), but no (0, v) with v irrational in (0,1), which is a limit of such q. ¬GloballyHyperbolic follows from it. A wording nit, prose of the REPORT only: 'meets {0} × ℝ in the rationals of (0, 1)' leaves out the endpoints (0,0) and (0,1), which are also rational. The Lean docstring (:714) is exact.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected/8-separation
labels.notes: I checked the 18 conjuncts of rationalJumpPlane_separates against the ladder's lean fields (programme/ladder.toml:248-379). In a probe, the 18-fold statement was written with full names: Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours rationalJumpPlane, Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal rationalJumpPlane.toPrecausality, …, ¬ Causal.Causality.GloballyHyperbolic rationalJumpPlane. `with_reducible exact rationalJumpPlane_separates` closed it. The theorem has no hypotheses and no instance arguments. #check also confirms the statements of rationalJumpPlane_zero_one_separates (≤ ⊤ (0,0) (0,1), and no causal curve for any W and s0 <= s1). It confirms the existential form: some C has AbsolutelyMinimalOn every W, ChronalNeighbours, CausallyOpen, HasTimeFunction, ¬LocallyCausallyArcConnected, ¬CausallyArcConnected, ¬LocallyPushUp and ¬CausallyPlain. It confirms the three bare forms: ¬ ∀ C on R × R with AbsolutelyMinimalOn every W, ChronalNeighbours and CausallyOpen, then C is CausallyArcConnected, resp. LocallyPushUp, resp. CausallyPlain. Their docstrings match. The plane decides all 18 causality-sort ladder properties: it has 12 and lacks 6.
